token.costGuideText: It's normal for ~90% of costs to come from cache (write + read). Curious why cache is essential and how to manage it?

chart.effNote: * Days with <1,000 output tokens are excluded (too small a denominator skews the ratio).
chart.effGuideLine2:
· Total / Output: total tokens divided by output tokens. Shows how many tokens are consumed on average to produce one unit of output.
· Cache Creation / (Input+Output): cache creation tokens divided by input+output tokens. Days with higher values likely had more cache expiry or session restarts. Since cache creation includes system prompts and tool results beyond just input and output, day-to-day trends are more meaningful than absolute values.
chart.effGuideLine3: 🆚 The gray line (before plugin) and green line (after) let you compare efficiency over time.
chart.hourlyNoteActive: * Active days: average cost only on days you actually used this hour.
chart.hourlyNoteAll: * All days: spread across every calendar day in the period (including days off).
chart.hourlyNoteMax: * Max: the highest single-day cost recorded for that hour.
chart.hourlyNotePartial: * Partial hours at the start/end are normalized to 1 hour (e.g., 20 min of data is scaled ×3).
chart.dowNoteActive: * Active days: average only on weeks you worked that day.
chart.dowNoteAll: * All days: divided by total occurrences of that weekday in the period (each weekday may have a different count).
chart.dowNoteMax: * Max: the highest single-week cost recorded for that day of the week.
chart.dowNotePartial: * Partial days at the start/end are normalized to 1 day (e.g., 6 hours of data is scaled ×4).
chart.ctxNote: * Lower context = cheaper per call. Keeping context small via /clear or /s-continue saves cost.
chart.ctxGuideLine2:
· CW option: calls where Cache Write was the dominant cost component. Cache creation is the most expensive token type, so it's separated for analysis. Dots at large context sizes indicate cache re-creation after 1+ hours of idle time. A single call can be costly — be careful.
· Non-CW option: calls where Cache Write was NOT the dominant cost. Usually Cache Read dominates, but since it gets a 90% discount, Output cost can be higher. Points above the price line typically occur during design docs or large code tasks — this is normal.
· User Turn option: AI makes multiple API calls per user question. This option aggregates all API costs for a single conversation turn to analyze per-question cost. Turns costing tens of dollars usually involve large-scale parallel or iterative tasks.
📈 As X-axis (context size) grows, caching (creation or reads) always occurs proportionally, so Y-axis (cost) increases. Refer to the price lines.
👆 Hover over any dot to see the prompt text, and the token count and cost breakdown for Input / Output / Cache Write / Cache Read.
chart.ctxCostTitleCW: 💸 Cost by Context Size — Cache Write (CW)
chart.ctxCostTitleNonCW: 💸 Cost by Context Size — Non-CW (Cache Read / Output)
chart.ctxCostTitleTurn: 💸 Cost by Context Size — Per User Turn
chart.ctxCostCWNote1: * Cache write is the most expensive token type — occurs when cache expires (1h+ idle) or after /resume, --continue.
chart.ctxCostCWNote2: * Each dot: an API call or user conversation, plotted by context size and cost.
chart.ctxCostCWNote3: * Lines: ── 1-hour cache write, ╌ 5-min cache write, ··· cache read.
chart.ctxCostCWNote4: * Dot/line colors: red tones = Opus, blue tones = Sonnet, green tones = Haiku.
chart.ctxCostNonCWNote1: * API calls where cache write is NOT the dominant cost (cache read, output, or input dominant).
chart.ctxCostNonCWNote2: * Each dot: an API call or user conversation, plotted by context size and cost.
chart.ctxCostNonCWNote3: * Dotted lines = cache read price per model. Points below may use a cheaper model.
chart.ctxCostNonCWNote4: * Dot/line colors: red tones = Opus, blue tones = Sonnet, green tones = Haiku.
chart.ctxCostTurnNote1: * Each bubble = aggregated cost of one user prompt (all API calls combined), sized by density.
chart.ctxCostTurnNote2: * ✳ Stars = turns exceeding $50 (capped for display — hover for actual cost).
chart.ctxCostTitle: Context Size vs High-Cost API Calls ($1+)

alert.compactAutoReason: /compact fired automatically due to context pressure. Cache was regenerated.
alert.pluginOverload: — too many plugins, MCP, or skills may be loaded. Keep only what you need.
alert.reloadReason: /reload-plugins caused system prompt change, cache regenerated (${cost})
alert.resumeHeuristicReason: Resuming a session with claude --continue or /resume uses a lot of tokens. Unless necessary, we recommend /s-continue skill after a new session.
alert.cacheExpiredReason: When context is large and over 1 hour has passed, new cache is generated — large cost!
alert.costCacheReadLabel: {icon} Cache read cost is high. Large context ({ctx}) with many consecutive tool calls ({calls}) multiplies cost. (${cost})
alert.costOutputReason: {icon} Output {tokens} dominated cost (${cost}) — consider using Edit (diff) instead of full file rewrites, and trim verbose explanations in your prompt.
alert.costInputReason: {icon} Input {tokens} dominated cost (${cost}) — consider using text instead of images, reading only needed sections with offset/limit, or providing summarized context.

gitLite.tip: Tip: CC's built-in git instructions consume ~2,200 tok/session + ~1,700 tok/call. `/setup-git-lite install` replaces them with a curated 280-tok minimum. `/setup-git-lite dismiss-banner` hides this tip.
